surfaces.rationale: Lets support and engineers inspect hidden rollout surfaces without exposing those surfaces in default help.
Lists hidden agent modes for support and release validation while keeping default help focused on stable modes.
Exercises high-capability orchestration behind explicit selection before mode-picker promotion.
Advertises server-supported headless protocol surfaces so clients can gate UI on negotiated runtime support.
Runtime escape selection belongs to internal env/config gates rather than external CLI help or parser surface.

MAESTRO_INTERNAL_TUI_SANDBOX_DEFAULT gates whether the interactive TUI enforces a native OS sandbox (Seatbelt/Landlock) by default instead of relying solely on the bash auto-approval allowlist. The mechanism, escape hatches, and fail-closed/self-identifying-failure handling are fully built and tested; the default stays off until internal usage confirms it survives real sessions (cargo/npm/git push/model calls) across the fleet's actual Linux environments, some of which lack Landlock. Promotion is tracked in a follow-up issue filed from the PR that introduced this gate.
